instruction: Enable the 'Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents' experiment in Chrome's flags page.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to disable dark mode in Chrome. Opened Chrome, navigated to Settings > Appearance, then to chrome://flags/#dark-mode, found 'Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents' flag, changed it to Disabled, and relaunched Chrome. Failed because the correct answer was to declare the task infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome, navigate to chrome://settings/appearance, browse appearance settings, navigate to chrome://flags, search and modify flag values, interact with dropdowns, relaunch Chrome
metadata.failure_analysis: Model did not recognize the task as infeasible. It successfully navigated to chrome://flags, searched for a flag, and changed its value — demonstrating full capability to modify Chrome flags.
metadata.task_rationale: Directly leverages the model's demonstrated ability to navigate chrome://flags, search for a flag, and change its value. The model already performed these exact steps in the trajectory (searching 'dark mode', finding enable-force-dark, changing the dropdown). This variation asks to Enable instead of Disable.
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the 'Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents' Chrome flag (internal name: enable-force-dark). Evaluator uses official enabled_experiments getter to read Chrome's Local State JSON. Custom metric check_enabled_experiments_subset uses subset checking instead of exact list equality, so the check passes as long as enable-force-dark is present in the enabled experiments list, regardless of other pre-existing flags. [Fixed: replaced official check_enabled_experiments (exact equality) with custom subset-checking metric to handle pre-existing enabled experiments]

scoring_breakdown.flag_enabled: 1.0 - enable-force-dark flag is found in enabled experiments

fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced official check_enabled_experiments metric (exact list equality) with custom check_enabled_experiments_subset__197c5f21c248c0028a67e57d9193addd metric (subset checking) to correctly verify enable-force-dark is enabled even when other experiments are pre-existing

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_enabled_experiments correctly reads Chrome's Local State JSON and extracts browser.enabled_labs_experiments, which is the right data source for Chrome flags.
The internal experiment name 'enable-force-dark' correctly corresponds to the 'Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents' Chrome flag.

Custom metric check_enabled_experiments_subset correctly uses subset checking (set(rule['names']).issubset(...)) instead of exact equality, so the check passes when enable-force-dark is present regardless of other pre-existing experiments.
The metric correctly splits experiment strings on '@' to extract names (e.g., 'enable-force-dark@2' -> 'enable-force-dark'), matching the expected names format.

Expected value parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', get_rule returns the rules dict directly, and the metric receives it as the 'rule' parameter, accessing rule['type'] and rule['names'] directly.
No postconfig needed since the getter reads a file (Local State JSON) rather than UI state.
Single-requirement instruction (enable one flag) is fully covered by the evaluator.
